source.title: Deductive Logic in Language Models: Horizontal vs. Vertical Reasoning

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses mechanistic analysis on synthetic deduction tasks to examine induction-head-like computation, rather than testing the original repeated-token in-context-learning task or its loss-based measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports direct mechanistic findings about induction-head-like retrieval and its development during training. It also discusses prior induction-head and phase-change results, which are cited background rather than results from this study. It does not measure later-token loss, in-context-learning curves, or a training-loss bump.
record.test_reason: The study trains small transformers from scratch on synthetic deduction tasks. It inspects attention, residual streams and Q/K/V contents, and finds induction-head circuits built on earlier token-copying heads. It also inspects checkpoints to track how these heads form. This is a new setting with direct results on V1, V2, V4, V5 and V7. It does not measure in-context-learning loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also state that the emergence of induction heads brings a sudden improvement, consistent with the phase-change finding, but that refinement may need several stages. They present induction heads as central to logical-inference circuits beyond text continuation.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes synthetic logical deduction and tree-navigation tasks with mechanistic circuit inspection, rather than testing repeated-token in-context learning or its loss-based measures.
record.method_sensitivity: CoT versus binary supervision and the Task 1 data-generation bias change whether the intended reasoning behavior or a shortcut is learned; Task 1 circuit development differs across training checkpoints.
record.problems: The mechanistic analysis centers on small, from-scratch models and synthetic symbolic tasks. The authors note that these methods may not transfer directly to larger pretrained models or naturalistic settings; the vertical path-merging mechanism is not fully understood. The additional-model comparison does not state its sample size. No ICL loss or training-loss bump is measured.

untested.parts: The canonical repeated-token [A][B]…[A]→[B] pattern on natural text. There is no causal or ablation evidence of composition; the analysis is passive inspection only.
In-context-learning measured as loss falling with token index, and the training-loss bump.
Entirely untested: no large models and no in-context-learning attribution.
Other model families, other architectures and other modalities. Non-converged runs were not inspected.
Persistence of in-context learning, and data properties other than CoT versus binary supervision and generation bias.
Sub-steps measured on in-context-learning loss, and transitions in other models.

missing.what: A 2-layer attention-only model trained on leaf-to-root Task 2 reaches 99.7% validation accuracy after 2 epochs, and induction-head circuits form. The root-to-leaf version reaches only 54%.
About 20% of 2-layer runs converged within 250 epochs, against 80% for the full architecture. Footnote 3 reports a similar two-plateau trajectory (20-30% and 60-80%) in other runs.
missing.locator: Section 5.1; Appendix C, footnote 3, Figure A1 (20 runs)

missing.what: Without CoT on unbiased data, Task 1 and Task 2 models memorise or fail to generalise (around 50-60% on Task 2). No mechanism inspection for induction heads is reported.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3: this is a new task setting, not a different method aimed at the original question. The reader's V4 limits_scope label was removed, because untested model families belong under untested, not limits_scope. All evidence comes from passive inspection, with no ablations. This study is not one of the original sources.

versions.untested_parts: The study examines induction-head-like completion and chaining in a small attention-only model, but does not test the canonical [A][B] … [A] → [B] pattern or explicitly establish composition with a previous-token head.
The study reports checkpoints for induction-circuit development and task accuracy, but does not measure in-context learning as later-token loss or a training-loss bump.
No large transformers or measure of most in-context learning are studied.

The study reports related behavior in configurations and tasks within one model family and mentions additional converged models, but does not test other model families, modalities, or broad universality.
The study compares CoT and non-CoT training setups and discusses a data-generation bias, but does not measure persistence of in-context learning.
The study does not measure few-shot task learning or compare it with copying behavior.
The reported stages concern development of the studied Task 1 circuits; the paper does not characterize transitions in other model families or in-context-learning loss.

rows.subject: 2-layer NanoGPT (Task 1), checkpoint t1
rows.operation_detail: Inspected induction-head-like rule-completion and rule-chaining circuits at an intermediate training checkpoint.
rows.value: Initial implementation present; works well only on initial implications in the chain.
rows.locator: Appendix C, discussion of Figure A2
rows.note: The authors suggest positional-encoding aspects may not yet be resolved.
rows.check: This is a formation checkpoint, not a measure of the mechanism, so the V1 link is dropped. The checkpoint sits at a task-accuracy jump (20%) and shows only partial induction heads.

source_check.correct: The epoch-30 induction mechanisms work only on initial implications. Partial is appropriate for incomplete formation relative to V2; the separate formation stage is observed relative to V7.
source_check.locator_found: Appendix C, Figure A2 discussion, first checkpoint bullet.
source_check.problem: A single partial state conflates incomplete induction mechanisms with positive evidence for V7's staged formation.

rows.subject: 6-layer NanoGPT (Task 2)
rows.operation_detail: Mechanistically described backward chaining at the last prompt position across layers.
rows.value: The model searches backward from the leaf to the root, retrieving a parent at each layer; the paper describes induction heads as central to this computation.
rows.note: The model reached 99.9% accuracy in about 50 epochs. The paper also reports that paths longer than model depth require partial paths to be merged, with those circuits not fully explained.
rows.check: Qualitative only, with no numbers for the induction-head analysis; 99.9% is task accuracy. The model has MLPs and 6 layers. Figure 6 uses an illustrative 5-layer model.

relationships.condition: 2-layer, 1-head, attention-only NanoGPT trained on Task 1 with CoT
relationships.reason: Layer-1 copy heads carry the expected token (average rank 1.072/1.011, r1-r2). Layer-2 search heads put 99.2%/99.8% of attention on the expected source (r3-r4). Q/K/V decode to the expected tokens at rank ≈1.0 (r5-r10).
relationships.display_finding: Layer-1 copy heads carried expected tokens at average ranks 1.072/1.011, layer-2 search heads assigned 99.2%/99.8% attention to expected sources, and query, key, and value vectors decoded expected tokens at approximately rank 1.0.
